description: Royal Straight Flush ♠️ — Five minds, one mission. We bring together AI, software, data, and creativity to solve space challenges at NASA Space Apps Challenge. Different skills, one hand, one goal: build something extraordinary.
summary:
1. Project Overview & Mission Context

Challenge: NASA Space Apps Challenge — Develop Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts.

Mission: Build an autonomous, visual health monitoring and clinical decision-support system for astronauts on long-duration missions across Low Earth Orbit, Lunar and Mars environments (up to 3-year missions).

Key Requirements:

Offline AI & Communication: Support local AI inference (LLM + TTS) during communication blackouts and queue medical data for asynchronous synchronization with Earth.
Dual-Audience Interface: Provide two modes: High-Level View, with simple explanations and guided self-examinations, and Technical View, with clinical telemetry, biomarkers, statistics and health trends for medical specialists.
Modular Frontend: Maintain a design-agnostic, decoupled architecture allowing UI layouts, themes and components to change without modifying business logic or API integrations.
Containerized Architecture & Cloud: Deploy the frontend and backend as separate, isolated containers, orchestrated through a root docker-compose.yml, with architecture designed for Google Cloud Platform (GCP) hosting.
details:
1. Project Overview & Mission Context
  • Challenge: NASA Space Apps Challenge — Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions.
    • 1. Communication Delays & Blackouts: Deep-space missions cannot rely on real-time Earth connectivity. The system must seamlessly fall back to local on-device AI inference (Local LLM + Local TTS) and queue telemedicine packets for asynchronous ground synchronization.
    • 2. Dual-Audience Accessibility: Astronauts are not always medical specialists. Every health metric, exam instruction, and risk assessment must support instant toggling between a High-Level View (plain-language guidance and step-by-step self-exam instructions) and a Technical View (clinical telemetry, biomarkers, statistical distributions, and raw trends for Crew Medical Officers and Ground Flight Surgeons).
    • 3. Modifiable & Scalable Frontend Architecture: Because the final visual UI/UX design has not been realized yet, the frontend architecture MUST remain strictly decoupled, modular, and design-agnostic so layouts, themes, and visual components can be swapped or scaled without rewriting business logic or API integrations.
    • 4. Containerized Multi-Service Architecture & Cloud Hosting: The entire application must be containerized with the Backend and Frontend running as two separate, isolated container services managed through a root Docker Compose configuration (docker-compose.yml), and architected to be hosted on Google Cloud Services (GCP).
2. Core Architectural Principles (Rules for All Agents)
  • Mandatory Documentation Tree (doc/) & Context Optimization:
    • All project documentation must reside inside a root doc/ directory following a tree-like structure that mirrors the codebase directories (for example: doc/front/general, doc/front/tts, doc/front/models, doc/back/api, doc/back/ai, doc/back/triage, doc/infra).
    • Every subdirectory inside doc/ must contain an index.md file that acts as a lightweight table of contents and router guiding future agents to read ONLY the required documentation files for their task so they do not fill their context window with unnecessary information.
    • Read Docs First & Update Immediately Rule: All future agents must ALWAYS read AGENTS.md and navigate the relevant doc/.../index.md files first before answering questions or modifying any part of the codebase. Whenever an agent modifies or adds code, it must update the corresponding documentation files inside doc/ (and index.md if files were added or removed) immediately in the same turn.
    • The frontend and backend must run as two separate container services orchestrated via Docker Compose (docker-compose.yml), each with its own Dockerfile and environment configuration.
    • The proposed hosting environment is Google Cloud Services (GCP) (including Cloud Run or GKE for containers, Artifact Registry for Docker images, Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL with pgvector and TimescaleDB, Vertex AI / Gemini API, Cloud Storage, and Secret Manager).
    • Separate Data/State Hooks (API fetching, caching, WebSocket streams) from Presentational Components.
    • Build every feature module (Astronaut Body Explorer, AI Companion, Telemetry Charts, Vitals Logger, Gachapon Engine) as an isolated, self-contained widget that can be rearranged in any grid, sidebar, modal, or tab layout as the final UI design evolves.
    • Use design tokens (CSS variables / Tailwind theme tokens) for all colors, spacing, and typography—especially for the standardized clinical status system: Nominal (Green), Caution (Amber), and Critical (Red).
3. Full Application Feature Specification

3.1 Frontend Modules (Modular & Layout-Agnostic)

  • Main Dashboard & Context Bar:
    • General Details & Mission Header: Crew member profile, mission day counter, active communication latency indicator, and overall Mission Readiness Score.
      • High-Level View: Plain-language explanations for non-medical astronauts, color-coded status badges, and step-by-step visual/audio instructions on how and why to perform self-measurements.
      • Technical View: Raw time-series telemetry, statistical baselines, biomarker breakdowns, confidence intervals, and clinical differential notes for medical personnel.
    • Clickable anatomical zones (Head/Eyes, Cardiovascular/Chest, Spine/Skeletal, Musculoskeletal/Limbs, Gut/Microbiome, Skin) displaying body part physiological functions, active health indicators, color-coded status (Nominal, Caution, Critical), and spaceflight-specific risks.
    • 3D avatar companion that visually speaks to the astronaut in real time, synced with ElevenLabs Integration (and Local TTS Fallback).
    • Renders custom equippable "skins" unlocked via the Gamification Engine.
    • Questions Chat: Interactive text and hands-free voice chat allowing astronauts to ask quick questions about their vitals, symptoms, or exam procedures.
    • Unified input module supporting manual numerical entry, simulated wearable streams, and camera/diagnostic media uploads:
      • Vitals: Blood pressure (systolic/diastolic), heart rate (bpm), blood sugar (mg/dL), body temperature, blood oxygen (SpO2).
      • Behavioral & Routine Logs: Daily sleep hours, sleep quality, mood/stress rating, nutrition/hydration intake, and exercise minutes.
      • Diagnostic Media: Camera uploads for skin rashes/lesions and simulated ultrasound/ocular scans.
    • Historic Health Trends: Dynamic, filterable charts tracking vitals over mission duration, overlaid with environmental events (radiation spikes, EVA sessions, gravity transitions).
    • Predicted Health Trends: Forecast trajectories generated by backend prediction models showing projected indicator paths and early-warning threshold crossings.
    • Routine Prompts: Automated checklist prompting scheduled checkups (morning vitals, pre/post-EVA checks, weekly behavioral surveys).
    • Gachapon Daily Checkup Reward System: Completing the daily scheduled health checkup awards a "Gachapon pull/throw" that unlocks collectible skins and visual customizations for the 3D AI Model Companion, alongside countermeasure streaks to combat isolation apathy.

3.2 Backend Services & Space Medicine Booster Modules

  • Hybrid LLM & RAG Clinical Engine:
    • Cloud LLM + Local LLM Fallback: Generates personalized Prevention Recommendations, High-Level Explanations, Technical Summaries, and powers Chat Mode for Quick Questions.
    • Vectorized Medical Knowledge Base (Database): Stores known spaceflight and terrestrial illnesses, their associated health variable vectors, exam protocols, and dual-layer (High-Level and Technical) descriptions grounded in NASA Human Research Program (HRP) evidence.
    • Prediction Model for Health Problems: Evaluates multi-variable vitals + environmental hazard weights to flag anomalies and calculate risk probabilities.
      • 1. Tier 1 — Self-Care & Preventative Countermeasure (Astronaut action).
      • 2. Tier 2 — Crew Medical Officer (CMO) Intervention (On-board clinical review).
      • 3. Tier 3 — Ground Flight Surgeon Alert (Packaged into the Asynchronous Telemedicine Sync Queue).
    • ElevenLabs Integration: Streams natural voice-over audio for LLM responses and hands-free exam guidance.
    • Local TTS Fallback: Automatically switches to local low-latency speech synthesis when offline or during simulated Mars communication blackouts.
    • 1. 5-Hazards Environmental Risk Matrix: Maps Location Setting + cabin habitability telemetry (temperature, pressure, lighting, noise, microbial counts) to physiological risk multipliers.
    • 2. SANS (Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome) & Fluid-Shift Module: Triggered via the Head/Eyes anatomical zone; tracks visual acuity, ocular ultrasound/camera scans, and prescribes countermeasures (e.g., Thigh Cuffs to retain fluids in lower extremities, B-Complex vitamin protocols).
    • 3. Autonomous Radiation (CANS) & Immune Viral Reactivation Monitor: Ingests simulated continuous Canadian Active Neutron Spectrometer (CANS) radiation dosimetry alongside stress/sleep logs and skin rash camera uploads to predict latent viral reactivation and microbiome shifts.
    • 4. EVA (Spacewalk) Decompression & Hypoxia Guard: Dedicated EVA prep/active mode monitoring decompression sickness ("the bends") protocols, mild hypoxia (SpO2 dips), CO2 buildup, and post-transition sensorimotor/vestibular readiness for manual vehicle piloting.
    • 5. Countermeasure Prescription & "Accelerated Aging" Tracker: Connects bone loss (osteoporosis risk), muscle atrophy, cardiovascular changes, and Type-2 diabetes/insulin shifts (blood sugar in mg/dL) to actionable prescriptions: Zero T2 non-treadmill exercise regimens, enhanced spaceflight diets, and Space Gardening tasks for psychological and nutritional resilience.
    • 6. Telemedicine Sync Packet ("Tempus Pro" Asynchronous Mode): Packages NASA Standard Measures, trend forecasts, and Tier-3 alerts into compact, prioritized JSON payloads queued for transmission to Earth Flight Surgeons whenever deep-space communication windows open.
  • Containerization: Docker & Docker Compose (docker-compose.yml) managing separate frontend and backend container services.
  • Cloud Hosting: Google Cloud Services (GCP) — Cloud Run / GKE, Artifact Registry, Cloud SQL (PostgreSQL + pgvector), Vertex AI, Secret Manager, and Cloud Storage.
4. Proposed Backend Integration Stack & API Boundaries
  • API Framework: Python (FastAPI) or Node.js (NestJS/TypeScript) exposing OpenAPI/Swagger REST endpoints + WebSockets for real-time telemetry and voice streaming.
    • Relational & Time-Series: PostgreSQL (with TimescaleDB for time-series vitals/telemetry and pgvector for vectorized illness descriptions and RAG retrieval) — or SQLite + ChromaDB/Qdrant for lightweight local hackathon deployment.
    • Primary Cloud LLM: OpenAI / Gemini / Anthropic API via unified LLM Router.
    • Local LLM Fallback: Ollama (Llama-3 / Phi-3 / MedGemma) running locally behind the same router interface.
    • Predictive ML: scikit-learn / XGBoost / Prophet (or lightweight statistical anomaly detection + ARIMA/rolling z-score models) for health trend forecasting and multi-variable risk scoring.
    • Primary: ElevenLabs Streaming TTS API.
    • Fallback: Local Piper TTS / Kokoro or browser-native offline TTS fallback flag.

Finalized Backend Stack & 4-Container Topology

  • 4-Container Docker Compose Topology (docker-compose.yml):
    • db (pgvector/pgvector:pg16): PostgreSQL 16 instance storing relational tables, time-series vitals telemetry, and pgvector embeddings for the NASA HRP medical knowledge base (maps to Google Cloud SQL).
    • ollama (ollama/ollama:latest): Local AI container with a persistent volume hosting medgemma (local medical clinical reasoning and multimodal ocular/skin image analysis) and nomic-embed-text (local text embeddings for 100% offline RAG).
    • backend (Python 3.11+ / FastAPI): Main API, scikit-learn ML inference, RAG, and voice gateway container exposing REST and WebSocket endpoints (maps to Google Cloud Run / GKE).
    • frontend (Isolated Container Service): Separate container service for the modifiable UI once the frontend stack is finalized (maps to Google Cloud Run).
    • API & WebSockets: FastAPI + Uvicorn (uvicorn[standard]), Pydantic, pydantic-settings, python-multipart (for image uploads), and httpx.
    • Database & Vector Store: PostgreSQL 16 + pgvector accessed asynchronously via SQLModel, SQLAlchemy (asyncio), asyncpg, and Alembic.
    • Hybrid LLM & Offline RAG: Google Cloud Vertex AI / Gemini API (google-genai SDK) as Primary Cloud LLM + Ollama (medgemma for medical generation and nomic-embed-text for vector embeddings) as Local LLM Fallback.
    • Predictive Machine Learning: scikit-learn, pandas, numpy, and joblib for Health Problem Classification and Health Trend Forecasting.
    • Voice Synthesis (TTS): ElevenLabs Streaming API (elevenlabs SDK) as Primary Cloud TTS + Local TTS Fallback (piper-tts / kokoro-onnx or browser offline speech synthesis flag).
    • Multi-Modal Media & Cloud Storage: Pillow (image validation/preprocessing) and google-cloud-storage (GCP media storage).
  • Backend Dependencies (requirements.txt): fastapi, uvicorn[standard], pydantic, pydantic-settings, python-multipart, httpx, sqlmodel, sqlalchemy[asyncio], asyncpg, pgvector, alembic, scikit-learn, numpy, pandas, joblib, google-genai, ollama, elevenlabs, Pillow, google-cloud-storage.

Core API Contract Endpoints (To Decouple Frontend & Backend)

  • GET /api/v1/context/location & POST /api/v1/context/location — Get/set active Location Setting, cabin telemetry, communication delay status, and 5-Hazard multipliers.
  • POST /api/v1/telemetry/ingest — Log multi-modal health indicators (vitals, sleep/mood, EVA metrics, or camera/ultrasound metadata) and trigger real-time triage evaluation.
  • GET /api/v1/astronaut/body-status — Return anatomical zone statuses (Nominal, Caution, Critical), active risks (e.g., SANS, Bone Loss), and dual-view (high_level and technical) descriptions.
  • GET /api/v1/trends/{indicator} — Return historic time-series data, mission event overlays, and predicted future trend points.
  • POST /api/v1/ai/chat — Send user health query + current context (view_mode: "high_level" | "technical", location, active vitals); returns structured answer, recommended countermeasures, triage tier, and audio stream URL/buffer (ElevenLabs or Local TTS).
  • POST /api/v1/gamification/checkup-complete — Validate daily checkup completion, increment readiness streak, and execute Gachapon roll returning unlocked 3D AI companion skin metadata.
  • GET /api/v1/telemedicine/sync-queue — Retrieve queued "Tempus Pro" Standard Measures packets awaiting Earth transmission.
